title: How To Build Deep Trust With Your New Class https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2016/08/27/how-to-build-deep-trust-with-your-new-class/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that trust is an overlooked but critical foundation of classroom management: when students genuinely trust a teacher, every other area of management becomes easier, and when they don't, nothing works as it should. He observes that teachers who consider themselves fully honest with adults often tell small "white lies" to students, over-praising undeserved work or overlooking misbehavior to avoid a hassle. He insists students notice this inconsistency and respond by becoming less motivated, less respectful, and more prone to misbehavior once they realize they can't count on the teacher's word. Building deep trust, he says, requires nothing more than consistently following through on promises and being truthful, not perfection. He closes by urging teachers to be a genuine "straight shooter" from the first week of school onward.
points: Trust is foundational: when students trust a teacher, virtually every area of classroom management gets easier.
Small dishonesties — inflated praise, ignored misbehavior to avoid hassle — erode student trust even though they seem harmless.
Students notice inconsistency between what a teacher says and does, and respond with reduced motivation and respect.
Building trust doesn't require perfection, just consistently following through on promises and being truthful.
quotes: It’s important because when your students trust you—really trust you— everything is easier.
Somewhere in the back of their mind, perhaps just outside of conscious awareness, they believe that telling little white lies here and there can’t hurt.
Because every time you play loose with the truth, every time you say one thing and do another, your students take notice. And it changes them.
Building deep and abiding trust, of the kind that inspires an almost reverent-like respect, is nothing more than following through on your promises and being truthful with your words.
Being a teacher of integrity doesn’t take great skill or effort. You don’t have to look or dress a certain way.
So make it a point this school year to do exactly what you say. Be real and transparent, a straight shooter , consistent in word and action.
